title: The Cost of an Unpredictable Delivery
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
A small manufacturer may pay more for a reliable delivery service than for a faster one. This can seem irrational if we compare only average journey times. Yet a business must organise workers and equipment before a shipment arrives. An unexpectedly early delivery can be troublesome if storage is limited, while a late delivery can leave an entire production line waiting.

An economist illustrated this problem through interviews with firms supplying wooden furniture to local shops. One transport company offered a short average delivery time, but arrival dates varied considerably. Another company usually took an extra day, although it supplied a narrow arrival window and warned customers promptly when that window changed.

Several firms preferred the second company. Their managers explained that a predictable timetable allowed them to reserve a loading area and arrange temporary workers for a single morning. With the faster service, they sometimes paid workers to wait or moved unfinished products to make room for an unexpected shipment. Those additional costs were not included in the delivery fee shown on the invoice.

The economist then compared records from businesses that had switched services. Waiting costs generally fell, but the savings were smaller for firms with large storage areas and permanent loading staff. Reliability had greater value where the business had little spare capacity to absorb a surprise.

This example does not establish that slower transport is usually better. Some goods lose value rapidly, and an urgent order may justify substantial uncertainty. It shows that average speed is only one part of service quality. When assessing a delivery system, we should also examine the spread of arrival times and the practical arrangements customers must make around them.

questions.prompt: Why might a firm prefer a slower delivery service?
options: Its goods become more valuable during transport.
Predictable arrivals make it easier to organise operations.
The firm is not allowed to compare delivery fees.
Slower vehicles always provide more storage space.
questions.answer: Predictable arrivals make it easier to organise operations.
questions.explanation: 稳定的到货时间有助于安排装卸场地和临时员工，减少运营成本。

questions.prompt: What distinguished the second transport company?
options: It delivered all goods on the day they were ordered.
It offered a narrow arrival window and timely warnings of changes.
It required customers to provide their own drivers.
questions.answer: It offered a narrow arrival window and timely warnings of changes.
questions.explanation: 第二家公司虽然平均慢一天，但到货窗口窄，变化时会及时通知。

questions.prompt: Which firms benefited more from a predictable service?
options: Those with little spare capacity to handle unexpected arrivals.
Those that never employed temporary workers.
Those whose shipments arrived without any unloading work.
questions.answer: Those with little spare capacity to handle unexpected arrivals.
questions.explanation: 缺少空余仓储和人员缓冲的企业从可靠性中获益更大。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker suggest including when judging delivery quality?
options: The colour of the transport company’s vehicles.
The average age of each customer’s workers.
The number of shops located near the warehouse.
Variation in arrival times and the arrangements it requires.
questions.answer: Variation in arrival times and the arrangements it requires.
questions.explanation: 结尾建议除了平均速度，还考察到货时间波动及客户为此所做安排。
